raw_response:
I've farmed these 12 mu for 30 years, and cotton is all I've ever grown here. I never went to school, but I know this soil and I know cotton. Last year the yield was decent, around 230 kg per mu, and this year I expect about the same if the weather holds. I'll plant my improved cotton seeds in late April when the ground warms up, just like I always do. I don't buy the expensive hybrid seeds; the improved ones from the village supply shop are good enough and I can afford them.

For fertilizer, I buy what I can afford and what has worked before. I'll put down compound fertilizer and urea before planting — roughly a bag and a half total per mu — and I'll spread more urea when the plants start flowering. I don't weigh it out in kilograms; I go by bags. Better to use a bit too much than too little, because if the yield drops, my wife and I suffer. There are only two of us, so we do all the work ourselves and we can't afford a bad year.

I'll irrigate twice from my well. Once after planting if the spring is dry, and again when the bolls are forming. Pumping costs electricity, so I don't water for nothing, but cotton needs that water at flowering or the bolls will fall off. I'll spray pesticide four times. The bollworm and aphids always come, and I walk the fields and spray when I see them. I till with the rotary tiller in spring to break up the soil before planting. If the weather is normal, I should get about 250 kg per mu.
